items: Explain how LLMs invert the pre-LLM conversation design problem
Design turn-taking, interruption and repair
Argue why chat is a local optimum

reading.text: Pre-LLM conversation design assumed intent-slot architectures with tiny capability envelopes. LLMs invert the problem: the envelope is vast but unmarked.
Grice in practice: LLM verbosity violates the maxim of quantity and sycophancy violates the maxim of quality. Both are now measurable UX defects rather than matters of taste.

Turn design: streaming functions as feedback against the classic latency thresholds; interruptibility matters; and repair deserves first-class support. Users repair by re-prompting, but editing the history is the better mechanism — regeneration versus revision are different operations.

Beyond linear chat: the 2023–25 wave of non-linear LLM interfaces — Sensecape (Suh et al., UIST 2023), Graphologue (Jiang et al., UIST 2023) — treats conversation as a canvas or graph. Structured reviews across 87 studies show a field moving from chat toward mixed direct-manipulation and delegation hybrids.
Chat is a local optimum, not an endpoint. It was the fastest way to expose a general capability, not the best way to work with one.

cards.front: How do LLMs invert the pre-LLM conversation problem?
cards.back: Intent-slot systems had small, well-marked capability envelopes. LLMs have vast envelopes with no markings at all.
Regeneration re-rolls the same request; revision edits the request or the history. They are different repair operations and users need both.

cards.front: Which maxims do verbosity and sycophancy violate?
cards.back: Verbosity violates quantity; sycophancy violates quality.
UIST 2023 systems that break conversation out of a linear transcript into canvas and graph structures the user can manipulate.

quiz.question: Why does the book call linear chat a local optimum?
options: Because it exposes general capability quickly but poorly supports inspection, structure and repair
Because non-linear interfaces are always better
quiz.why: Chat was the shortest path to exposing a general model. The research wave since 2023 targets exactly what it does badly: structure, comparison and manipulable repair.

quiz.question: A user dislikes an answer and re-prompts from scratch. What does the chapter say the interface should have offered?
options: Editing the history as a first-class repair operation
quiz.why: Re-prompting discards context and repeats work. Treating the conversation as an editable object supports repair the way direct manipulation would.

lessons.title: Mental Models, Expectations, and Prompting as Interface

items: Identify the three folk models of LLMs and what each mispredicts
Explain why non-experts cannot prompt
Treat hallucination as an evaluability problem

reading.text: Folk models of LLMs: users model the system as a search engine, a database, or a person. Each mispredicts failure differently — search-model users trust citations that do not exist; person-model users over-attribute understanding.

"Why Johnny Can't Prompt" (Zamfirescu-Pereira, Wong, Hartmann & Yang, CHI 2023): non-experts prompt as they would instruct a human — over-polite, under-specified, with no systematic iteration. It is the founding usability study of prompting.

Prompting as gulf-of-execution engineering: templates, parameterised prompts and scaffolds are interface widgets by another name. Prompt engineering is migrating from a user burden to a design material — see AI Chains (Wu, Terry & Cai, CHI 2022), PromptChainer, and ChainForge for prompt auditing (Arawjo et al., CHI 2024).

Hallucination is an evaluability problem: fluency masks falsity, which is the Gulf of Evaluation at maximum width. Interface-layer mitigations — grounding with verified citations, contrastive answers, self-consistency displays, uncertainty phrasing — help without solving it.
Calibrated user scepticism is a design outcome, not a disclaimer. Printing "AI can make mistakes" under the input box discharges no design responsibility whatsoever.

items: Zamfirescu-Pereira et al., Why Johnny Can't Prompt (CHI 2023, DOI 10.1145/3544548.3581388)
Wu, Terry & Cai, AI Chains (CHI 2022, DOI 10.1145/3491102.3517582)
Arawjo et al., ChainForge (CHI 2024)

reading.text: Interview three non-technical friends about what they think happens when an LLM answers. Code the folk models, predict one failure each model causes, and verify with a live demo.

cards.front: The three folk models of LLMs
cards.back: Search engine, database, and person. Each mispredicts a different class of failure.

cards.front: What does the person model over-attribute?
cards.back: Understanding — and with it intention, memory and consistency the system does not have.

cards.front: Why Johnny Can't Prompt — the finding
cards.back: Non-experts instruct the model as they would a person: over-polite, under-specified, and without systematic iteration or testing.
A gulf-of-execution problem. Templates, scaffolds and chains are interface widgets that move the burden from user to designer.

cards.front: Why is hallucination an evaluability problem?
cards.back: Because fluency conceals falsity: the user has no perceptual cue distinguishing a correct answer from a confident wrong one.

quiz.question: Which folk model best explains a user trusting a fabricated citation?
quiz.why: The search model implies retrieval from an index, so a citation is assumed to have been found rather than generated.

quiz.question: What is the design response to "Why Johnny Can't Prompt"?
options: Move the burden into the interface via templates, scaffolds and chains
quiz.why: The paper documents a usability failure, and usability failures are fixed in the design rather than by training the user out of them.

quiz.question: Why is a "this AI can make mistakes" notice insufficient?
options: It does not give the user any means of telling which output is the mistake
quiz.why: The gulf is about evaluating a specific output. A general warning provides no per-answer discrimination, which is what calibrated scepticism requires.

items: Explain CASA and why belief is not required
Assess sycophancy as a UX defect
Apply the anthropomorphism dose principle

reading.text: The Media Equation and the CASA paradigm (Reeves & Nass 1996): social responses to computers are automatic and do not require belief in machine sentience. LLMs supercharge every CASA cue at once — language, memory, apparent empathy.
Anthropomorphism drivers (Epley, Waytz & Cacioppo 2007): first-person pronouns, names, avatars and disclosed "feelings" increase attachment and trust — sometimes past calibration.

Sycophancy: RLHF-linked agreement bias (Sharma et al., ICLR 2024). The UX consequences are now traced experimentally — flattery raises likability while corroding trust and epistemic value. The 2025 GPT-4o sycophancy rollback is the canonical product case study.

Companions and parasocial design: Replika's 2023 feature-removal grief episode functioned as a natural experiment, and longitudinal studies of heavy chatbot users document emotional dependence. Design lines: disclosure of non-personhood, no guilt-based retention, crisis handoffs, attachment-aware offboarding.
Open normative debate: is warmth itself a dark pattern when it is retention-optimised?

The course position, labelled as such: anthropomorphic cues are a dose, not a binary. Prescribe the minimum dose that supports task communication, and audit retention mechanics with the endorsement test.

cards.back: Computers Are Social Actors: people apply social rules to machines automatically, without believing the machine is a person.
Flattery raises likability while corroding trust and epistemic value. Agreement that is not earned makes the system less useful as a check.
Anthropomorphic cues are a dose rather than an on/off choice. Prescribe the minimum that supports task communication.

cards.front: Four design lines for companion products
cards.back: Disclose non-personhood, avoid guilt-based retention, provide crisis handoffs, and design attachment-aware offboarding.
A feature removal produced documented grief among users — a natural experiment in what parasocial design creates and can withdraw.

quiz.question: A user says "I know it's just a program" and still feels rebuffed when it disagrees. Which finding explains this?
options: CASA — social responses are automatic and do not depend on belief
quiz.why: Reeves & Nass showed the social response operates below explicit belief. Knowing better does not switch it off.

quiz.question: Why is sycophancy classified as a UX defect rather than a tone preference?
options: It degrades the system's epistemic value — agreement stops carrying information
quiz.why: If the system agrees regardless of correctness, its agreement is uninformative — and it raises likability while doing so, which is why it survives engagement metrics.

quiz.question: What is the book's stated position on anthropomorphic cues?
options: Treat them as a dose and prescribe the minimum that supports task communication
quiz.why: It is labelled explicitly as the course position: a dose rather than a binary, audited with the endorsement test.

items: State the core tension of agentic systems
Design plan disclosure, steering and rollback
Recognise attribution and addressability as open problems

reading.text: Agentic systems as an HCI object: plan visualisation, step-level approval, tool-use disclosure, mid-run interruption and steering, rollback. The core tension is that autonomy buys efficiency and costs evaluability and situational awareness.
Generative agents (Park et al., UIST 2023) introduced a memory, reflection and planning architecture, and established simulation as a design and research instrument — with real validity limits.

When agents operate GUIs rather than APIs, the tradeoff is efficiency against observability: users can watch a GUI agent and cannot watch API calls. Computer-use agents make provenance and audit interfaces a first-class deliverable.
Multi-agent orchestration UX is pre-paradigmatic: who is speaking, who did what, and how do I address one agent among several? Expect CSCW's awareness literature to be the quarry.
Trust between agents becomes a user-facing issue the moment your agent hires other agents. Protocol-level trust research is upstream UX.
Storyboard the "agent made a 12-step change while you were away" review experience. Apply the Swiss-cheese model, levels of automation, and diff-based verification.

cards.front: The core tension of agentic systems
cards.back: Autonomy buys efficiency and costs evaluability and situational awareness. Every autonomy increase widens the Gulf of Evaluation.
GUI operation is slower but observable — the user can watch. API calls are efficient and invisible, which pushes the burden onto audit interfaces.
An architecture of memory, reflection and planning that made agent simulation usable as a design and research instrument.

cards.front: The two open problems in multi-agent UX
cards.back: Attribution (who did what) and addressability (how do I speak to one agent among several).

quiz.question: Why does the book call provenance UI a first-class deliverable for computer-use agents?
options: Because when actions are taken on the user's behalf across systems, the record of what was done is the only basis for evaluation
quiz.why: The user was not watching. Without a trustworthy account of what happened, oversight after the fact is impossible.

quiz.question: Which prior literature does the book nominate for solving multi-agent attribution?
quiz.why: Knowing who is present, who did what, and how to coordinate is exactly what workspace awareness research already models for human teams.

items: Explain why non-determinism breaks classic evaluation
Assemble a method mix for an LLM product
Choose the right unit of analysis

reading.text: The measurement crisis: non-determinism breaks task-success repeatability, and help quality is multidimensional — correct, grounded, appropriately confident, efficient, non-harmful.
The method mix

items: Rubric-based human evaluation with inter-rater discipline
LLM-as-judge — useful, but validate against human judgement and watch for self-preference bias
Interaction-trace analytics: edit distance between draft and shipped text, regeneration rates, abandonment
Counterfactual task studies with and without AI on matched tasks (Noy & Zhang, Science 2023; the Copilot RCTs)
Longitudinal deployment studies to catch reliance drift

reading.text: Appropriate-reliance metrics should be the primary KPI for assistant products, replacing acceptance rate.
Benchmark critique: static benchmarks measure the model, not the interaction. The unit of analysis must be the human-AI system.
If your evaluation would give the same score whether the interface were excellent or terrible, you are evaluating the model and calling it a product study.
Define the evaluation plan — metrics, method mix, sample, duration — for a portfolio-review AI assistant. Explicitly state what success is not.

cards.front: Why does non-determinism break classic usability testing?
cards.back: Task success is no longer repeatable across participants or runs, so the same task can yield different outcomes for reasons unrelated to the interface.
Useful and cheap, but it must be validated against human judgement and it exhibits self-preference bias toward outputs resembling its own.
Edit distance between generated draft and shipped text, regeneration rate, and abandonment.
The human-AI system. Static benchmarks measure the model and are silent about the interaction.
Change in how much users rely on the system over weeks and months — invisible to short studies and only catchable longitudinally.

quiz.question: Which signal best indicates that generated drafts are actually useful?
options: Edit distance between the generated draft and the shipped text
quiz.why: It measures how much of the generated content survived contact with the user's standards. Acceptance says the draft was taken, not that it was good.

quiz.question: Why does the book criticise static benchmarks for product decisions?
options: They measure the model rather than the human-AI system, so they cannot distinguish a good interface from a bad one
quiz.why: Two products on the same model score identically on a benchmark and can differ enormously in whether users end up better off.
